title: Is Text All You Need? Text as a Universal Information Bottleneck for Speech LLMs
claim: Speech features are bridged to a frozen text-embedding space by constraining each frame to a convex mixture of token embeddings.
layout: Multi-region left-to-right flow with colored dashed modules; convex-hull geometry inset below
description: A wide architecture diagram split into colored, dashed-border regions. At top left, an audio waveform feeds a gray Whisper Large-V3 encoder (snowflake icon for frozen). The encoder output is pooled and passes into a large blue 'Convex Gate (C-Gate)' region. It holds three white boxes with equations: query projection, full-vocabulary softmax scoring, and a convex mix over TopK-16 embeddings. Flame icons mark the trainable boxes. An orange panel at bottom left shows the frozen LLM embedding table E as stacked rows. Lines from it supply K and V to the gate. A green panel at bottom center sketches the convex hull: scattered points, vertices E1–En, and a star for the mixed embedding. A yellow 'LM Modeling' panel at bottom right shows text-prompt and pseudo-embedding tokens entering Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct.
caption: C-Gate Architecture. A sparse convex mixture of frozen token embeddings connects the speech encoder to the partially adapted decoder. Snowflakes mark frozen modules, and flames mark components with trainable parameters. Decoder adaptation is restricted to the attention projections specified in Section [ref].
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) provide a powerful reasoning backbone for speech understanding, but integrating continuous acoustic signals into a pretrained LLM remains challenging. A central design question is how to tie speech representations to the LLM's text input space while preserving the continuous variation needed for different speech tasks. In this work, we propose Convex Gate (C-Gate), a speech-LLM bridge that represents each frame as a convex combination of frozen token embeddings. This architectural convex-hull constraint fixes the output codebook while allowing continuous mixtures learned from task supervision. With a Whisper-large-v3 encoder, a partially adapted Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct decoder, and joint training on speech recognition, emotion recognition, and spoken reasoning, C-Gate performs accurate transcription and emotion recognition, our representative semantic and acoustic tasks, through one shared decoder. On text-only benchmarks, the adapted decoder loses instruction-following and MMLU accuracy and matches or exceeds the original model on GSM8K and HellaSwag. We further design analyses and interventions on the trained model to examine where the bridge sequence carries task information and how the decoder reads it. These findings show how fixed text embeddings can support both semantic and acoustic readouts through continuous speech-conditioned mixtures.
